newsitem.title: GERMANY: Controversial German reactor gets foundation stone.
newsitem.headline: Controversial German reactor gets foundation stone.

text.p: About 50 people protested on Monday as the foundation stone was laid for a controversial German nuclear research reactor which the United States says could boost nuclear proliferation.

The reactor at Garching, near Munich, will be the first outside China and Libya created to use highly enriched uranium -- which can also be used in the construction of nuclear warheads -- since an international drive to curb use of the fuel began in 1978.
Anti-nuclear activists staged a peaceful protest outside the site, which will be used by Munich's Technical University.
Bavarian state education minister Hans Zehetmair said the 767 million mark facility, to be built by Siemens AG, would prove its value both in research and for practical uses including medicine.
The 20-megawatt reactor, a fraction of the size of commercial power plants which average about 1,000 megawatts, will be used by the university for neutron research and to produce cancer medicines.
Germany argues it needs the reactor to remain a world leader in these fields.

But the United States has made no secret of its irritation over the reactor, which it regards as a blow to its efforts to stem traffic in weapons-grade nuclear fuel and reduce the risk of proliferation.
U.S. officials say use of the reactor is likely to have the knock-on effect of enriched uranium being imported to western Europe from Russia and the former Soviet Union.
Construction at the site began last August and it is due to be finished in 2001.
